reviewed_by: Codex focused review for Butler project lifecycle plus workflow registry source guard
reason: Fifteen collected Python cases retain the 11 Butler project lifecycle, durable retry, knowledge-index and Chroma checks and add four Node-backed registry checks: current UI call inventory, detected call drift, rejection of false supported status, and refusal of invented Core catalog operations. Sixty-six listed frontend cases remain selected for the project lifecycle candidate. The frontend production build now runs the source guard as prebuild and is required in CI. Eight paired browser profiles retain the authenticated production-LAN Butler project journey. The registry/docs slice changes no runtime workflow; its own checks are source-level. The Python CI install condition now includes the selected registry test file, so its Node-backed checks receive the UI TypeScript dev dependency before test execution; the previous CI job proved Node was present but the dependency install was skipped. The selected 15 Python checks and frontend build directly verify this setup repair on a fresh runner.
exclusions: No native source changed, so no native tests are selected. Unrelated Python, frontend, and Playwright journeys are excluded. The registry scans calls on the variable named api and is explicitly an incomplete action map; unreviewed signatures do not imply Butler support. Browser profiles emulate mobile devices; physical Safari is unavailable. The name guard applies to Butler keyed creates; unkeyed project creation retains existing semantics. The CI workflow change only widens dependency installation for this exact selected Python file; it does not change product runtime or require unrelated browser journeys.
